claims.text: A machine-learning predictive approach will identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity more accurately than conventional empirical or simplified computational methods.
The proposed model uses high-dimensional descriptors of atomic structure, bonding, and lattice dynamics.
The target materials are primarily random-solid-solution high-entropy alloys synthesized under controlled conditions.
The model is trained on experimental high-entropy-alloy datasets containing measured phonon thermal conductivities.
Local bonding environments and lattice dynamics mediate phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys.
Bonding, atomic mass, and lattice disorder interact nonlinearly to influence phonon scattering.
The machine-learning model can capture the complex nonlinear interactions among atomic-level descriptors that influence phonon scattering.
Capturing these atomic-level interactions will improve phonon thermal-conductivity predictions relative to conventional approaches.
The proposed approach will reduce phonon thermal-conductivity prediction error by at least 15% relative to current empirical or simplified computational models.
The approach is applicable to single-phase, random-solid-solution high-entropy alloys whose compositions are well represented in the training data.
The approach may not generalize to non-HEA materials, extreme temperatures, or non-equiatomic compositions outside the training domain.
A 15–25% improvement in prediction accuracy is anticipated based on preliminary evidence.
Failure to obtain at least a 15% reduction in prediction error relative to conventional models across the tested alloy series would falsify the hypothesis.
